subject: Clarification on peering maintenance exclusion and uptime impact
messages:
From: Jonathan Lin <jonathan.lin@wavehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Partial regional errors during EdgeLink peering maintenance

Hi Kimberly,

We saw a sustained spike in 5xx errors and tail latency across our US-west cluster between 2027-08-27 22:40 and 2027-08-27 23:55 UTC (request ids and traces attached). Our stack-level monitoring indicates the pattern coincides with a scheduled maintenance notice we received from our transit partner, EdgeLink, where they performed a peering table refresh that affected a subset of prefixes into us-west.

WaveHealth is evaluating the customer impact. Could you confirm how Redwood treats partner peering maintenance for uptime calculations? EdgeLink's notice explicitly lists a maintenance window; they claim the routing changes were planned but their update caused packet drops for ~75% of affected flows. We need to understand whether that window will be excluded from our SLA uptime calculation, and if not, how Redwood is apportioning responsibility when a third-party peering event causes partial degradation.

Attached: WaveHealth sample request IDs (wavehealth-request-samples.log) and EdgeLink maintenance notice (EdgeLink-notice.pdf).

Thanks,
Jonathan Lin
Head of SRE, WaveHealth
ops@wavehealth.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jonathan Lin <jonathan.lin@wavehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partial regional errors during EdgeLink peering maintenance

Hi Jonathan — thanks for the report and the attachments. We're sorry to hear some of your traffic experienced errors.

Quick answers up front: Redwood excludes scheduled maintenance windows that are recorded in our maintenance ledger from uptime calculations, but third-party peering events are handled differently — we first verify the timeline and then apportion any availability hit to the subset of traffic paths that are demonstrably impacted.

To help us validate, please populate the attached request-ids-template.csv with a representative sample of full request IDs (start/end timestamps are sufficient) and the client IPs observed. That will let our telemetry and routing teams correlate your traces with our ingress egress logs and the EdgeLink BGP flaps you referenced.

I'll triage this to ops and routing; looping in Marissa (CS/ops) for the SLA side and Ben for any potential commercial remediation.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
From: Jonathan Lin <jonathan.lin@wavehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Aug 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partial regional errors during EdgeLink peering maintenance

Kimberly — attached is the CSV populated with samples and a short log bundle (wavehealth-request-samples.log). The timestamps are in UTC; the EventIDs column maps to traces in our APM.

EdgeLink's notice is included; note they scheduled maintenance from 2027-08-27 22:30 to 2027-08-27 23:15 UTC, but our observations show a tail that stretched to ~23:55 UTC as routes reconverged and traffic rebalanced. We consider this a third-party peering-induced partial degradation rather than a full Redwood maintenance window.

Let us know what you find and if you require anything else. If Redwood will not exclude that tail, please explain the attribution methodology so we can escalate internally.

— Jonathan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonathan Lin <jonathan.lin@wavehealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partial regional errors during EdgeLink peering maintenance

Hi Jonathan — thanks for the samples and the EdgeLink notice; we completed a cross-team review (routing, telemetry, and ops). Below is a concise summary of our findings and the resulting SLA impact determination.

Executive summary:
- EdgeLink performed the scheduled peering change from 2027-08-27 22:30 to 2027-08-27 23:15 UTC (their notice matches).
- Our telemetry shows Redwood saw increased 5xx rates for a subset of egress prefixes beginning ~22:40 UTC and returning to baseline by ~23:55 UTC.
- During EdgeLink's listed window (22:30–23:15 UTC), 54% of the error volume is attributable to transit routing changes that match EdgeLink's AS-path updates. The remaining error volume in that span correlates with transient queueing on our side (failed retries and elevated queue drains).
- Between 23:15–23:55 UTC (post-notice tail), the error volume was concentrated on ~3/12 of our peer paths; these errors were caused by residual BGP reconvergence and repeated transient drops as traffic migrated. We classify that tail as mixed-cause (third-party + local path reconvergence).

How we apply exclusions and credits:
1) Scheduled maintenance recorded in our internal maintenance ledger is fully excluded from uptime calculations. (This does not apply here because EdgeLink's notice is from a third party and was not surfaced to our ledger in advance.)
2) For third-party incidents, our policy is to apportion the availability impact only to the fraction of traffic demonstrably affected. We compute this by correlating request-level success rates across ingress prefixes and weighting by observed traffic volume.
3) For this event, after weighting, we attribute roughly 67% of the total error-time impact to EdgeLink's peering change and 33% to internal reconvergence/backoff behavior.

Outcome and remediation offered:
- Calculated effective uptime hit for WaveHealth for that UTC day: 0.48% (after apportionment).
- Per our SLA, we will apply a pro-rata usage credit equal to 0.48% of that month's hosted inference fees, subject to WaveHealth confirming the linked HubSpot record and accepting the standard credit form.
- Because this was a mixed-cause event, we are also providing a complimentary routing workshop with our infra team to help reduce reconvergence exposure if WaveHealth would like.

Attachments: redwood-uptime-explainer.pdf (walkthrough of our apportionment method).

Next steps:
- Jonathan: confirm whether you accept the proposed credit and the routing workshop. If so, we'll raise the credit through our billing flow (HubSpot: HS-0004192) and send DocuSign for the acceptance.
- Kimberly/Ben: I'll follow up with a short root-cause note to include in the incident ledger so future scheduled third-party maintenance can be coordinated ahead of time.

Thanks — appreciate the samples; they were critical to the apportionment.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Customer Operations — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-uptime-explainer.pdf
